narrativeReportMd:
# MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
R6 no longer provides a `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` resource StructureDefinition. The comparable R6 representation appears to be `ClinicalUseDefinition` with `type = undesirable-effect`, which makes this a high-impact resource identity and content-model migration rather than an in-place evolution.

## Scope
I compared the R4 resource against the R6 package index and the R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition` StructureDefinition. Inherited base-resource changes are excluded.

## Main migration themes
Existing R4 instances need a resourceType change, a required type discriminator, at least one subject, and nesting of the former top-level undesirable-effect fields under `undesirableEffect`. `subject`, `symptomConditionEffect`, and `population` also change representation types.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact issues are the removal/merge of the resource identity, mandatory `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` and `subject`, path movement into an `undesirableEffect` backbone, and replacement of inline `Population` with `Reference(Group)`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for confirming the official merge path, mapping R4 `MedicinalProduct` references to R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition`, deciding how to externalize `Population` into `Group`, and handling the new modifier `status`.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many individual data points can be migrated, but the replacement resource intentionally consolidates several clinical-use concepts. A less disruptive design could have retained the old resource as a deprecated alias/profile while introducing `ClinicalUseDefinition`.

## Follow-up analysis
A full cross-version ConceptMap or IG guidance would materially improve migration confidence, especially for references, population conversion, and status semantics.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` is absent as an R6 resource and appears to have been merged into `ClinicalUseDefinition`. Top concerns are resource identity breakage, required `type` and `subject`, moved fields under `undesirableEffect`, and conversion of `Population` to `Reference(Group)`. The main uncertainty is the absence of an official cross-version diff or ConceptMap.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is not a field-by-field rename only. R4 data must be transformed into `ClinicalUseDefinition`, set `type` to `undesirable-effect`, move effect details under the `undesirableEffect` backbone, convert subject references to R6 target choices, and decide how to represent population and status. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy for new target types, `CodeableReference.reference`, `status`, `management`, `library`, and other added elements.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the computable changes because the R6 package index lacks the assigned StructureDefinition and the R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition` snapshot contains the undesirable-effect backbone and discriminator constraints. Confidence is lower for committee intent and preferred migration mechanics because no official diff, ConceptMap, or narrative change note was available locally.

findings.title: R4 resource identity is absent in R6 and appears merged into ClinicalUseDefinition

semanticText.definition: Describe the undesirable effects of the medicinal product.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 instances use `resourceType: MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` and the canonical StructureDefinition URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect`.

newState.summary: No R6 StructureDefinition for `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect`; likely replacement is `ClinicalUseDefinition`.

semanticText.definition: A single issue - either an indication, contraindication, interaction, undesirable effect or warning for a medicinal product, medication, device or procedure.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 package index contains `ClinicalUseDefinition` but no `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` StructureDefinition. Undesirable effects are represented as `ClinicalUseDefinition` records with `type = undesirable-effect` and an `undesirableEffect` backbone.

facts.note: The old resource type is not present as an R6 StructureDefinition.

facts.newValue: Merged multi-purpose clinical-use resource with a required type discriminator

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 package has no assigned `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` StructureDefinition. `ClinicalUseDefinition` explicitly includes an `undesirableEffect` backbone and the `undesirable-effect` type code, making it the strongest local counterpart.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A conformant R4 instance with `resourceType: MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` will not validate as an R6 resource because that resource type is absent. Generated model classes, REST endpoints, search parameters, FHIRPath expressions, subscriptions, and profile URLs keyed to the old resource name all need migration. R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition` instances are not cleanly representable as R4 `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` unless they are specifically the undesirable-effect branch and unsupported R6 content is discarded or extended.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Undesirable-effect data can affect medicine safety labeling and decision support. Dropping or misclassifying records during a resource identity migration could affect warnings and downstream pharmacovigilance workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate indication, contraindication, interaction, undesirable-effect, and warning concepts into one clinical-use resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` as a deprecated concrete R6 resource while also introducing `ClinicalUseDefinition`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Consolidating related clinical-use concepts into `ClinicalUseDefinition` is a coherent R6 goal, especially because the new resource shares subject, status, population, and branch mechanics across indications, contraindications, interactions, warnings, and undesirable effects. The breakage is high because resource type, canonical identity, generated classes, and APIs change. A less-breaking transition existed, but it would have compromised the clean single-resource model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest less-breaking base design would keep a concrete, deprecated `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` resource in R6 while adding `ClinicalUseDefinition`; a profile or alias over `ClinicalUseDefinition` alone would not preserve R4 `resourceType` validity. That alternative preserves most R4 instances, but creates a long-lived duplicate representation and requires servers, search definitions, validation, and migration guidance to handle both resource identities.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve old instances and endpoints, but leave parallel resources, search surfaces, and conformance expectations for the same clinical-use fact.

evidence.detail: R4 defines the concrete resource `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect`.
No R6 StructureDefinition entry for `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` was found; only `ClinicalUseDefinition` and `MedicinalProductDefinition` matched the related resource search.
`ClinicalUseDefinition` is defined to cover undesirable effects among other clinical-use issues.
evidence.quote: A single issue - either an indication, contraindication, interaction, undesirable effect or warning...

examples.examplesMd: The example is illustrative and focuses on the identity and container change. A production transform must also populate a valid `subject`.

findings.narrativeMd: The resource is not simply renamed in place. R6 removes the old concrete resource identity from the core package and represents undesirable effects through a branch of `ClinicalUseDefinition`. This is a hard break for validators and model libraries that dispatch on `resourceType`, canonical URL, or generated class name.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `resourceType: MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` is old-valid/new-invalid under R6 core because R6 has no such resource StructureDefinition. Conversely, a generic R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition` cannot be assumed to be an R4 undesirable effect unless `type = undesirable-effect` and only mappable fields are present.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create an explicit resource-level transform. Change `resourceType` to `ClinicalUseDefinition`, set `type` to `undesirable-effect`, move old fields to the R6 paths described in the other findings, and preserve the old identity in provenance, source metadata, or a cross-version extension if round-tripping matters. Test serializers, API routing, search, profile canonical references, and generated model dispatch.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The consolidation likely improves reuse across related medicine safety concepts, but it could have been less disruptive if the old resource stayed as a deprecated alias/profile. Because R6 has chosen a different resource identity, implementers need an explicit migration rather than schema-only validation.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The replacement is inferred from local computable definitions. Official change notes or a ConceptMap should be checked before freezing production migration rules.

findings.title: R6 requires a type discriminator and local constraints for the undesirable-effect branch

oldState.summary: Dedicated R4 resource had no local `type` element.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 resource identity itself implied that the instance described an undesirable effect.

newState.summary: R6 requires `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` 1..1 with required binding and enforces branch consistency.

binding.description: Overall defining type of this clinical use definition.

constraints.human: ClinicalUseDefinition.undesirableEffect can only be used when type is 'undesirable-effect'
Indication, Contraindication, Interaction, UndesirableEffect and Warning cannot be used in the same instance

newState.narrativeMd: `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` must be present and must be one of the required codes. The undesirable-effect backbone is only valid when `type` is exactly `undesirable-effect`.

facts.oldValue: No branch discriminator constraints on the R4 resource
facts.newValue: cud-1 through cud-6 enforce one branch and type/backbone consistency

impact.impactRationaleMd: A migrated R4 undesirable-effect record that omits `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` or uses any value other than `undesirable-effect` with the `undesirableEffect` backbone will fail R6 validation. The change is straightforward to populate, but it is a required field with a required binding, so schema-only or naive resource renames are insufficient.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: An incorrect discriminator can cause an undesirable effect to be processed as a different clinical-use issue or rejected.

justification.inferredGoal: Disambiguate the branch used inside the merged `ClinicalUseDefinition` resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make `type` optional or infer it from the populated branch, or avoid needing it by retaining separate clinical-use resources.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: For the chosen merged-resource design, a required discriminator is reasonable because consumers need to know which clinical-use branch is active and base constraints enforce branch/type consistency. The value is deterministic for migrated R4 undesirable-effect records. The less-breaking paths reduce the immediate validation break only by weakening the merged model or by retaining old resource identities.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Within `ClinicalUseDefinition`, R6 could have allowed `type` to be omitted when `undesirableEffect` is present and inferred the branch from the backbone, with profiles or warnings requiring explicit type. That would help some naive migrations, but it does not preserve raw R4 instances and leaves branchless or partially populated instances less explicit. Keeping the old resource would avoid the discriminator entirely, but has the duplicate-resource tradeoffs described in the root finding.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Optional or inferred typing weakens uniform base validation and search; separate resources duplicate the model surface.

evidence.detail: `type` is 1..1, code, required-bound to `clinical-use-definition-type`.
The required code system includes `undesirable-effect` meaning side effects or adverse effects associated with the medication.
The `undesirableEffect` backbone is constrained to instances whose type is `undesirable-effect`.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 record has no explicit type; the R6 migration must add it.

findings.narrativeMd: The old resource used its resource name as the discriminator. R6 uses one resource for several clinical-use concepts, so a required `type` code now carries that identity. This affects validators, generated enums, FHIRPath rules, and business logic that previously did not need to inspect a field to know the record kind.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old data is not valid as R6 unless transformed to include `ClinicalUseDefinition.type = undesirable-effect`. R6 validation also rejects an instance that has `undesirableEffect` with another type or combines multiple clinical-use branches. R6-to-R4 conversion can usually drop the type after confirming it is `undesirable-effect`, but other type values are outside this R4 resource's scope.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Set `type` deterministically to `undesirable-effect` for every migrated record from this R4 resource. Add validation tests for missing type, wrong type, and multiple branch backbones.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The discriminator is a necessary part of the merged design. A backward-compatible path would have kept separate resource identities or made `ClinicalUseDefinition` additive while deprecating the old resource, but that would not provide one uniform base model.

findings.title: Subject became mandatory and changed from Reference to CodeableReference with different target resources

oldState.narrativeMd: An R4 undesirable-effect instance could omit `subject`, and if present it referenced either `MedicinalProduct` or `Medication`.

newState.summary: R6 `subject` is mandatory 1..* `CodeableReference` to a wider target set, with `MedicinalProductDefinition` replacing `MedicinalProduct`.

binding.description: A coded concept that defines the type of a medication.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires at least one subject and permits either a coded concept or a reference to a broader set of product, device, substance, nutrition, biologically-derived product, activity, or plan definitions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The min cardinality increase is a direct validation break: an R4 instance with no `subject` can be valid in R4 but cannot produce a valid base R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition`. The type change also breaks generated code and transforms that expect a `Reference`; R6 `CodeableReference.concept` and the added target resource types have no direct R4 slot.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The subject identifies what product or therapy the undesirable effect applies to. Missing or incorrectly mapped subjects can attach a safety effect to the wrong product class.

justification.inferredGoal: Require every clinical-use issue to identify its applicable product, substance, device, procedure, or plan and support coded subjects.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `subject` optional and retain an old Reference-compatible representation while adding coded or broader subject support separately.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The subject is central to safely interpreting an undesirable effect, and the broader `ClinicalUseDefinition` scope reasonably needs product, device, substance, procedure, and coded subject support. The cardinality increase is nevertheless a hard break for subjectless R4 records. A less-breaking base design exists, but it has material safety and interoperability tradeoffs because it would continue to allow incomplete base records.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could leave base `subject` at `0..*`, keep a Reference-compatible form for migrated R4 `Medication` and legacy medicinal product references, and require subject through profiles, warnings, or implementation guides. That alternative only partially meets the R6 goal: it does not guarantee that every base clinical-use issue identifies its subject, and it still needs a policy for the R4 `MedicinalProduct` to R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition` target shift and for coded subjects.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves subjectless records but permits base R6 safety data without a subject and complicates old/new target and coded-subject handling.

evidence.detail: R4 `subject` is 0..* Reference to `MedicinalProduct` or `Medication`.
R6 `subject` is 1..* CodeableReference with a widened target profile set.

examples.examplesMd: R4 allowed no subject. R6 also allows coded subjects, which cannot be represented as an R4 `Reference` without an extension or manual mapping.

findings.narrativeMd: `subject` is both more mandatory and structurally different. Migration has to backfill missing subjects, wrap references inside `CodeableReference.reference`, and decide how to map R4 `MedicinalProduct` references to R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance omitting `subject` can become invalid in R6. Existing R4 instances with `Medication` references are structurally mappable after wrapping, but `MedicinalProduct` references require target-resource migration. R6 instances using `CodeableReference.concept` or new target resource types cannot be represented in R4 `subject` without loss or extensions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit all R4 records for missing subjects. For present `Medication` references, map to `ClinicalUseDefinition.subject.reference`. For `MedicinalProduct`, coordinate with the `MedicinalProductDefinition` migration and preserve source identifiers. Define a policy for coded R6 subjects if round-tripping to R4 is required.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The cardinality increase has a clear safety rationale, but old incomplete data could have been tolerated by keeping the base element optional and adding profile-level requiredness. The target widening is useful in R6 but adds unavoidable round-trip loss for non-R4 target forms.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm the project-specific mapping from R4 `MedicinalProduct` to R6 `MedicinalProductDefinition`; this report did not analyze that resource pair in depth.

findings.title: Former top-level effect fields moved under ClinicalUseDefinition.undesirableEffect

oldState.summary: Effect details were top-level local elements on the R4 resource.

newState.summary: Effect details are nested under the R6 `undesirableEffect` backbone.

constraints.human: ClinicalUseDefinition.undesirableEffect can only be used when type is 'undesirable-effect'

newState.narrativeMd: R6 introduces `ClinicalUseDefinition.undesirableEffect` 0..1 as the container for the old effect detail fields.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element names and definitions closely match: `classification` and `frequencyOfOccurrence` keep their names, and `symptomConditionEffect` keeps its name while changing type.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Top-level JSON properties from R4 are not valid at the top level of R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition`; they must be nested. This breaks serializers, generated accessors, FHIRPath expressions, patch paths, search extraction code, and JSON-schema-like validation that uses old paths.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If effect details are not moved, migrated records can lose the actual adverse-effect description or be rejected.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate the undesirable-effect branch from other branches inside the merged `ClinicalUseDefinition` resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain root-level undesirable-effect detail fields as deprecated base aliases while adding the `undesirableEffect` backbone.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A branch backbone is a natural content model for a resource that can carry several mutually exclusive clinical-use branches. The move is disruptive for JSON paths, generated accessors, FHIRPath, and patch/search logic, but it keeps the merged resource structurally coherent. The less-breaking alternative has material duplicate-representation costs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A true base-design alternative would allow `symptomConditionEffect`, `classification`, and `frequencyOfOccurrence` at their old root-level locations when `type = undesirable-effect`, not merely as extensions or profile guidance. That would preserve old paths after the resource-level migration, but validators and consumers would need rules for root-versus-backbone precedence, and deprecated parallel paths could persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Old paths would survive, but the same facts could appear at root and under the backbone, requiring precedence and cleanup rules indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 defines the three effect detail elements directly under the resource.
R6 defines corresponding fields under `ClinicalUseDefinition.undesirableEffect`.

examples.examplesMd: The example omits required R6 wrapper fields such as `resourceType`, `type`, and `subject` so the path movement is clear.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 moves the undesirable-effect-specific properties under a branch backbone. Even where names and cardinalities are retained, code using old property paths will fail until the data is wrapped in `ClinicalUseDefinition.undesirableEffect`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 top-level fields become invalid at their old locations in R6. R6 content can usually be unwrapped back to R4 for these three fields, subject to the separate `CodeableReference` change for `symptomConditionEffect`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Implement a deterministic path transform for `symptomConditionEffect`, `classification`, and `frequencyOfOccurrence`. Update FHIRPath expressions, JSON patches, search extraction code, serializers, profile differential paths, and generated model accessors.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The move is explainable by the resource merge. A compatibility profile or old-path extension could reduce migration pain, but would not allow base R6 validators to accept old JSON paths.

findings.title: symptomConditionEffect changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference(ObservationDefinition)

oldState.summary: R4 uses `CodeableConcept` with no local binding.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represents the symptom, condition, or undesirable effect as a codeable concept only.

newState.summary: R6 uses `CodeableReference(ObservationDefinition)` with an example binding.

binding.description: An undesirable effect of clinical use.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 permits either a coded concept or a reference to an `ObservationDefinition`, allowing richer reusable definitions but changing the JSON shape and generated type.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `CodeableConcept` content can usually be migrated into `CodeableReference.concept`, so the type change is not independently a hard data loss for coded/text content. It is still a runtime and codegen break because accessors, JSON shape, and validation type differ. R6 references to `ObservationDefinition` cannot be represented in R4 without resolving or extension-preserving the reference.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The field describes the adverse symptom or condition; losing a referenced definition or mishandling concept text can change clinical meaning.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow undesirable effects to be represented by reusable observation definitions as well as inline coded concepts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the `CodeableConcept` field and add an optional `ObservationDefinition` reference sibling or other additive reference support.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing an undesirable effect to be represented by a reusable `ObservationDefinition` is reasonable, and `CodeableReference` is the standard R6 pattern for concept-or-reference content. Existing R4 concepts can be represented through `CodeableReference.concept`, so the data goal is mostly preserved, but the wire shape and generated type still change. A less-breaking design exists but carries duplicate-representation and ambiguity costs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept `symptomConditionEffect` as `CodeableConcept` and added a separate optional reference, such as a sibling reference element, for reusable `ObservationDefinition` content. A choice element would not fully preserve old JSON unless the old name and shape were retained. The additive sibling would protect R4 concept instances, but systems would need clear precedence and validation rules if both concept and reference were populated, and the old representation might never disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves concept values and old generated types, but creates two representations for the same effect and requires rules when both are present.

evidence.detail: R4 type is `CodeableConcept`.
R6 type is `CodeableReference` targeting `ObservationDefinition`.
The R6 example ValueSet uses a SNOMED filter, but no expansion was present locally.

examples.examplesMd: A concept can be wrapped under `concept`; a reference-only R6 value requires a policy for R4 export.

findings.narrativeMd: This change is less hard than the resource identity or subject requiredness changes, but it matters for generated model code and round-trip conversion. R4 consumers expecting a `CodeableConcept` will not find one at the R6 path without unwrapping `CodeableReference.concept`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: After the path migration, old concept content can remain valid by wrapping it as `CodeableReference.concept`; therefore this is not counted as an independent hard instance break. However, R6 `CodeableReference.reference` values are not R4-representable in the old field without resolving to a concept or using an extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap R4 `symptomConditionEffect` as `ClinicalUseDefinition.undesirableEffect.symptomConditionEffect.concept`. For R6-to-R4 export, decide whether to resolve `ObservationDefinition` references to a concept, carry a contained/resource extension, or flag records for manual review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding a separate optional reference would have preserved old generated types, but R6's `CodeableReference` pattern provides a single standard representation for concept-or-reference fields.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology expansion was unavailable, so no conclusions are made about specific code removals or additions.

findings.title: population changed from inline Population datatype to Reference(Group)

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 embeds age, gender, race, or physiological population qualifiers directly in each undesirable-effect resource through the `Population` datatype.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 points to one or more `Group` resources rather than carrying inline population qualifiers.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance with inline `Population` content cannot be placed directly into R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.population`; R6 expects a `Reference(Group)`. Migration must create or find suitable `Group` resources and replace inline content with references. R6 references cannot be losslessly round-tripped to R4 inline population fields unless the referenced group is resolved and mapped.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Population qualifiers can affect which patient cohort an undesirable effect applies to, so lossy conversion can alter clinical interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Reuse `Group` for population definitions and avoid duplicating population criteria inline.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain inline `Population` as a legacy option while adding `Reference(Group)`, or add a separate Group reference alongside the old field.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Switching to `Reference(Group)` supports reusable population definitions and avoids embedding population criteria in each clinical-use record. The R6 package does not contain the old `Population` StructureDefinition, so retaining it in base R6 would be a broader compatibility concession. Because inline R4 population data cannot validate as a Group reference, the break is real; however, the less-breaking alternatives have material normalization, referential-integrity, and duplicate-representation tradeoffs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep the old inline `Population` field and add a `Group` reference, or define a legacy-preserving choice/sibling model. That would preserve R4 instances, but it would require rules for when inline criteria and referenced `Group` disagree, would keep legacy population criteria in circulation, and would still leave R6-to-R4 export lossy when only an unresolved `Group` reference is available.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves old inline data but retains an old datatype absent from R6 and creates duplicate population representations that can diverge.

evidence.detail: R4 `population` is 0..* with type `Population`.
R6 `population` is 0..* Reference targeting `Group`.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example assumes a corresponding `Group` resource has been created or identified.

findings.narrativeMd: `population` changes from embedded qualifier data to a reference. This is a representational break with operational consequences: migrated bundles may need new `Group` resources, stable identifiers, and referential integrity management.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 inline `Population` objects are not valid as R6 `Reference(Group)` values. R6 `Group` references cannot be exported to R4 without resolving group criteria and mapping them into the older datatype or preserving the reference as an extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all R4 `population` uses. Define a deterministic conversion from each inline population qualifier to a `Group` resource or to a shared canonical group. Validate that referenced groups are included or resolvable in bundles and that R6-to-R4 export has a policy for unresolved groups.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This change was likely avoidable from a compatibility perspective because an additive reference or choice could have supported both models. The chosen R6 model reduces duplication but shifts complexity to resource management.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The internal `Population` and `Group` definitions were not deeply assessed here under the base/referenced-artifact scope rule.

findings.title: R6 adds optional modifier status that can change interpretation of the issue

oldState.summary: R4 resource had no local `status` element.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` has no local lifecycle/status modifier for whether an issue is current or retired.

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that can indicate that a record should not be treated as valid

newState.narrativeMd: `status` can indicate that a record should not be treated as valid, so R6 consumers cannot safely ignore it when present.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The new element is optional, so it does not invalidate old R4 instances during R4-to-R6 migration. It is still a high runtime risk for R6 consumers and R6-to-R4 converters because modifier elements cannot be ignored safely. R4 has no equivalent local field, so status values can be lost or must be carried by extension.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Treating retired or non-current clinical-use information as active could affect medication safety workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent lifecycle state for clinical-use issues.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: optional `status` is additive for R4-to-R6 instances and does not require a less-breaking base alternative.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A lifecycle status is reasonable for reusable clinical-use knowledge, and the element is optional, so migrated R4 instances are not invalidated by its absence. Marking it as a modifier is also reasonable because retired or inactive status can change whether the issue should be treated as valid. The residual risk is mainly R6 consumer behavior and R6-to-R4 down-conversion, not R4-to-R6 base-instance compatibility.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A non-modifier status would reduce generic consumer obligations, but would understate the safety-relevant meaning of inactive or retired content. Because this is optional R6 content and a modifier/down-conversion concern rather than a hard R4-to-R6 design break, backward-compatible alternative availability is not applicable.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No old-instance preservation tradeoff; R6 consumers and R6-to-R4 converters must preserve or honor modifier semantics.

evidence.detail: R6 `status` is 0..1 CodeableConcept with `isModifier = true` and a preferred publication-status binding.

evidence.detail: No local R4 `status` element exists on `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect`.

examples.examplesMd: R4 has no native field for this modifier status; preserving it requires extension or side-channel metadata.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a lifecycle status that is explicitly a modifier. This does not break old data on input, but it changes how R6 records must be interpreted and raises safety risk for systems that ignore unknown or unmapped fields during conversion.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 instances remain migratable without status. R6 instances with status are valid R6 but not natively representable in R4 `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect`. Runtime consumers must check status before acting on the issue.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6 migration, decide whether to leave status absent or derive it from source governance metadata. For R6-to-R4 export, use an extension, provenance, or reject records whose status changes interpretation if the target system cannot honor it. Add tests that retired/inactive status values do not drive active warnings.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The element is optional, so the design is backward-tolerant for old data. The modifier flag is semantically appropriate but forces R6-aware consumers and converters to handle it deliberately.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The exact code set and business meaning depend on the publication-status ValueSet and local policy.

findings.title: R6 adds example bindings for undesirable-effect detail fields

oldState.summary: R4 effect detail elements had no local terminology bindings.
oldState.narrativeMd: `symptomConditionEffect`, `classification`, and `frequencyOfOccurrence` were unconstrained by local bindings in the R4 StructureDefinition.

newState.summary: R6 adds example bindings for symptom, classification, and frequency fields.

binding.description: R6 example bindings include undesirable-effect-symptom, undesirable-effect-classification, and undesirable-effect-frequency.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local ValueSets identify systems and filters, but no expansions were present. Because all bindings are example strength, validators should not reject non-member codes solely because of these bindings.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 provides example terminology guidance for the mapped fields, including SNOMED-filtered ValueSets for symptom and classification and an internal frequency ValueSet.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Example bindings do not create base validation failures for codes outside the ValueSet, so this is not a hard instance-breaking change. The risk is conformance, UI, code generation, or quality tooling that treats example bindings as stronger guidance or assumes expanded code lists.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Terminology guidance can influence display and categorization, but the bindings are not required.

justification.inferredGoal: Provide terminology guidance for undesirable-effect coding without making it mandatory.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding example bindings improves terminology guidance while preserving existing local codes and text. Because example-strength bindings do not make non-member codes invalid in base R6, the change is already compatibility-preserving for validation purposes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The chosen example-strength binding is already the less-disruptive alternative to required or extensible binding. No separate backward-compatible base design is needed; implementers should only ensure validators and code-generation tools do not treat example bindings as closed code lists.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No base validation tradeoff; only tooling that overinterprets example bindings may need adjustment.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: example-strength bindings are non-restrictive guidance and do not break base R4-to-R6 validation.

evidence.detail: The R4 local effect detail elements have no binding.
R6 adds example bindings for symptom, classification, and frequency.
ValueSets were present but expansions were not included locally.

examples.examplesMd: No instance example is needed because example bindings do not make non-member codes invalid in base R6.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 supplies more terminology guidance for undesirable-effect fields. This is useful for implementers but not a hard validator break because the binding strength is `example`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 codes outside the R6 example ValueSets remain base-valid after migration, assuming the structural transform is correct. Tooling that materializes enums or warnings from example bindings should be checked so it does not accidentally reject legacy coding systems.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not drop or recode existing values solely to satisfy example bindings. If harmonization is desired, use terminology services, ConceptMaps, or local coding policy, and test systems that display or classify undesirable effects by these ValueSets.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The design is appropriately backward-compatible because it adds non-restrictive guidance. Stronger bindings would have been more breaking; the example strength avoids that.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Expansion-level comparison was not possible with the local package alone.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: No local fixed, pattern, or default values were found on the compared R4 elements or their R6 undesirable-effect counterparts.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limits were identified on the compared elements.
No local slicing was found on the R4 resource elements or the R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.undesirableEffect` branch.

The mapped undesirable-effect detail elements remain summary elements in R6. New R6 elements such as `status`, `identifier`, `category`, `management`, and `library` are summary elements, but no old local summary element appears to have lost summary status.

No required or extensible binding was added to the old undesirable-effect detail fields. R6 adds example bindings only; expansions were not available, so terminology impact is limited to guidance/tooling risk.

The material local R6 constraints are the `ClinicalUseDefinition` branch/type invariants captured in the findings. No additional local constraints were found on the mapped `classification`, `frequencyOfOccurrence`, or `population` fields beyond inherited `ele-1` rules.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional undesirableEffect.management
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `management` is optional 0..* and therefore does not invalidate migrated R4 records that lack it.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6-to-R4 export has no native R4 field for management actions; preserve by extension or accept loss if the receiving workflow does not need management guidance.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional identifier, category, and library elements around clinical-use issues
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: These elements are optional additions and do not make old data invalid.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: They may be useful targets for source identifiers, classification metadata, and computable logic during R6 enrichment. They are not natively represented in R4 `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Replacement resource scope widens beyond medicinal products and medications
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: A broader R6 semantic scope is not itself an R4-to-R6 validation break for migrated undesirable-effect records.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 records may apply to devices, substances, nutrition products, biologically derived products, activities, or plans, so systems that assume medicine-only semantics should check `subject` targets.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: This report uses `ClinicalUseDefinition` as the likely R6 replacement but does not assess all branches or cross-branch behavior in depth.
R4 `subject` could reference `MedicinalProduct`, while R6 uses `MedicinalProductDefinition`; reference migration needs that artifact's own breaking-change analysis.
R4 inline `Population` values need conversion to R6 `Reference(Group)`; the exact lossiness depends on `Population` and `Group` semantics.
